name: KS-04

model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Estes: a heavily Republican seat, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge, with markets pricing a Republican win near certainty. With no polls or ratings available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of roughly fifteen points Republican.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Tyndell within single digits, or a surge of Democratic outside spending, would be the first sign of a real contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kansas's fourth district is a solidly Republican seat, and incumbent Ron Estes is seeking another term after easily clearing his primary. His Democratic challenger, Katy Tyndell, has raised only about $234,000 and had roughly $73,000 on hand, while Estes has raised $1.86 million and holds $1.76 million in cash. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's Republican lean, Estes's incumbency and financial dominance, and prediction markets that give him about a 93 percent chance of winning. A Democratic upset would require a major, currently unseen shift in the political environment.
